rv.q: This is a humorous, well-crafted piece which deserves its extended outing.
The Constant Wife is a witty and thoughtful production that reminded me a little of Oscar Wilde or George Bernard Shaw around the edges.
The Constant Wife is quite possibly the best play I’ve ever seen.
The Constant Wife is funny, set in the 1920s it is still able to resonate today and is a joyous and upbeat night out despite the themes of infidelity and betrayal.
The Constant Wife is gentle rather than raucous comedy, well-played and constantly entertaining – well worth a visit, this one!

cn.t: Critics praise Laura Wade's sharp, sparkling adaptation of Maugham's comedy of manners for its consistently witty dialogue and Kara Tointon's central performance, finding it both funny and surprisingly layered in its satire of privilege.
